title: sdks: unify auth/retries + streaming ergonomics across python/typescript/go and bump versions
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: bring parity across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs for auth token refresh, retry/backoff configuration, and streaming ergonomics. This PR unifies helper APIs, standardizes defaults, and bumps package versions across SDKs so users get consistent behavior and migration surface is minimal.

Summary of changes: standard auth helper (token refresh + caching) added to all SDKs; introduced a shared RetryPolicy abstraction (max_attempts, initial_backoff, max_backoff, multiplier, retriable_statuses) and exposed builder-friendly APIs; added a unified streaming iterator/async iterator API that hides connection lifecycle and provides clearer backpressure semantics; bumped Python -> 1.8.0, TypeScript -> 2.5.0, Go -> v0.9.2; docs and quickstarts updated with migration notes.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement auth token helper in python/typescript/go
- [x] Standardize retry/backoff defaults and validate with unit tests
- [x] Add streaming iterator helpers + examples
- [x] Update docs (docs/sdk-migration.md) and quickstarts
- [x] Run CI across all SDKs and address flakes
- [x] Bump package versions

Notes on compatibility/migration: Most surface area is additive. Key behavioral change: retry default initial_backoff reduced to 100ms (was 250ms in some SDKs) to match server SLO targets; token cache TTL default set to 10m (previously 30m) to reduce stale token windows for short-lived credentials. Migration guide has recommended config snippets for teams who want previous behavior.

CI: All SDK unit tests, linting, and integration tests were run. There was a transient race in Go streaming CI that required an extra sync on close; fix applied and re-run.

Related: closes ENG-4218 (SDK parity), ENG-4239 (streaming ergonomics), references SUP-78 for a support ticket that requested consistent retry behavior across SDKs.
